clue.text: The depth one may sink to as a sailor

definitions.text: The depth one may sink to as a sailor

parts.words: The depth one may sink to as a sailor
parts.note: reads like a sailor's moral decline, but describes how deep a vessel sits in the water, with a nod to the sailor sinking a drink

explanation.surface: A warning about how low a seafaring man might fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's draught is the depth of water its hull sinks to; a draught is also a drink a sailor might down.

clue.text: Record is within a couple of figures

indicators.note: the word within tells us one piece sits inside the other piece here

parts.note: D and C are two Roman numerals, 500 and 100
taken as written

explanation.surface: A claim that a record lies between two numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figures' reads as numbers in general, but here they are Roman numerals: D is 500 and C is 100.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record, the vinyl platter that holds music.

clue.text: Prophet leaves seafarer well off

indicators.note: the prophet leaves, so that word's letters depart from the longer word

parts.note: a seer is a prophet who foresees the future

explanation.surface: A soothsayer abandons a mariner who is wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes S, E, E, R out of SEAFARER in order, leaving AFAR. 'Well off' looks like rich, but here it means a long way off.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means at a great distance, and well off can mean far away in space.

clue.text: Adventurous men of old who went to the top at sea

definitions.meaning: dashing, bold gentlemen of former times, chivalrous adventurers

definitions.text: who went to the top at sea
definitions.meaning: topgallant sails and masts are set high up on a sailing ship, above the topsails

explanation.surface: Daring men of a bygone age who climbed the rigging.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense hangs on topgallants, the sails set above the topsails, so the word sits under 'top' on the mast.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallants were spirited, dashing men of earlier centuries, and the gallant sails sit near the top of a ship's rigging.

clue.text: Building quarters within a rock

indicators.note: the word within places the quarters inside the rock in this clue

parts.note: a tor is a rocky outcrop on a hill, as on Dartmoor
W and E, west and east, are two quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Lodgings carved out inside a crag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarters' looks like housing, but means compass points; a tor is a rocky hilltop, common on Dartmoor in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower is a tall structure, so it is a kind of building.

clue.text: Fights for leftovers

definitions.meaning: brawls or scuffles, informal for minor fights
remnants of food or material that are left after use

explanation.definitionFit: Scraps are both small scuffles and bits of leftover food, two unrelated senses of one word.

clue.text: A recipe swallowed in remedy for poison

indicators.note: being swallowed in the remedy signals that the letters go inside it

parts.note: a cure is a remedy for an illness
R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on old prescriptions

explanation.surface: A doctor's prescription gulped down as an antidote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowed in' puts A and R inside CURE. R is the old prescription mark meaning 'take'.
explanation.definitionFit: Curare is a plant extract poison used by South American hunters on arrow tips.

clue.text: Garden parties?

parts.note: the garden is Eden and the parties are the two people who lived there

explanation.definitionFit: The first man and woman lived in the Garden of Eden, so they were the parties in that garden.

clue.text: One way and another I'll stop

parts.note: ST, street, is a common abbreviation for a way
taken as written
another way, so a second ST for street
the apostrophe is ignored, giving the letters as written

explanation.surface: A frustrated driver tried one road then another and gave up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' stands for a second way, so ST appears twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A standstill is a complete halt, when all movement stops.

clue.text: Partition between pigs and birds

indicators.note: the partition goes between, so it sits inside the pigs in this clue

parts.note: sows are female pigs
a wall is a partition dividing a space

explanation.surface: A farm fence separating the pigsty from the poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partition' looks like the definition of a divided space, but it is just one piece; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Swallows are migratory birds with forked tails.

clue.text: A jolly girl Philip sent to sea?

parts.note: a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A cheerful young woman whom a man named Philip packed off on a cruise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' is old naval slang for a Royal Marine. Philip II of Spain sent his fleet against England in 1588.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish fleet of 1588 was dispatched by King Philip II, so it is what Philip sent to sea.

clue.text: He's far out once more

indicators.note: out here means in disarray, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the apostrophe is dropped, leaving the letters as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has wandered off into the distance yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges HES and FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Afresh means anew or again, starting over once more.

clue.text: Girl we hear presuming to transfer figures

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, so the girl's name stands for a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Carrie is a girl's name
forward means presumptuous, bold or overfamiliar

explanation.surface: A bold young woman is gossiped about as she takes liberties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' makes the name Carrie stand for CARRY, which sounds the same. 'Presuming' is an adjective here, as in being forward.
explanation.definitionFit: In bookkeeping, to carry forward is to move a total to the next page or period.

clue.text: Developed reliance on ship

indicators.note: developed means worked into a new form, so the letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Dependence on a vessel has grown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Developed' rearranges RELIANCE and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean liner is a large passenger ship crossing the open sea.

clue.text: Game for an old school get-together

definitions.meaning: a sport, the fifteen-a-side ball game
a reunion of former pupils of Rugby, the English public school

explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is a famous English boarding school where the sport is said to have begun, so its old boys' reunion is a play on words.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby union is the fifteen-player code of the sport; read differently it is a meeting of Rugby School alumni.

clue.text: Legal compulsion to be a suitor?

definitions.meaning: a binding instruction issued by a judge
an instruction, read as a command, telling someone to woo

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the phrase as a command: an order to court, that is to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: A court order is a judge's binding direction; read as a command, it is an order to go courting, as a suitor does.

clue.text: Fame made owner change name

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of the words get altered in order

explanation.surface: The proprietor altered his title for the sake of celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges OWNER plus N; 'made' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown is widespread fame or celebrity.

clue.text: Stop that girl!

definitions.meaning: a full stop, the punctuation mark
A girl's name, short for Dorothy

explanation.definitionFit: A dot is a full stop in punctuation and also a short form of Dorothy.

clue.text: Egg producer's supply at capacity

indicators.note: capacity read as acting in another capacity, so the letters take on a different role and order

explanation.surface: A poultry farm's output is running at full stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capacity' rearranges SUPPLY and AT; ''s' is a link. The surface suggests a hen farm, but the egg layer is a mammal.
explanation.definitionFit: The duck-billed mammal of Australia is one of the few mammals that lays eggs.

clue.text: A pound put on for service

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: Someone has gained some weight in time for church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' is a church service and 'put on' means worn.
explanation.definitionFit: An alb is a white ankle-length vestment that a priest wears for celebrating Mass.

clue.text: Not inclined to be fair

definitions.meaning: flat, not sloping at an angle

explanation.definitionFit: Something level is not tilted, and the idiom means honest and fair dealing.

clue.text: The French always turn up for this show

indicators.note: in a down clue, to turn up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: la is French for the, feminine
ever means always

explanation.surface: French people always arrive for a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reverses LA and EVER, giving LAEVER read upwards. 'Turn up' looks like arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal is to show or disclose something hidden.

clue.text: A bay of victory?

parts.note: not a stretch of coastline but leaves of the bay tree, woven into a garland for winners

explanation.definitionFit: A garland of bay leaves was placed on the heads of victors in ancient Greece and Rome.

clue.text: Make a run for the match

definitions.text: Make a run for the match

parts.words: Make a run for the match
parts.note: sounds like cricket, but means running away to get married, the match being a marriage

explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run off secretly in order to marry, and a match is a marriage.

clue.text: The dance lacks nothing in tastefulness

indicators.note: the dance lacks a piece, so those letters are removed from it

parts.note: the tango is a Latin American ballroom dance
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: The dancing is without any refinement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks' removes O (nothing) from TANGO. 'Tastefulness' means fullness of flavour, not good taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Tang is a sharp, strong flavour, a fullness of taste.

clue.text: Destroys ambitions

definitions.meaning: finishes off or puts an end to
aims or goals one is working towards

explanation.definitionFit: To end something is to destroy it, and ends are the aims one pursues.

clue.text: Fixed form of denial

indicators.note: a new form of the word means its letters are reshaped into another order

explanation.surface: A settled kind of refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges DENIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Nailed means fastened in place, fixed with nails.

clue.text: Grumble, having malady that's never-ending

indicators.note: never-ending means without an end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a complaint is an illness or ailment

explanation.surface: A grouse from someone with a chronic illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never-ending' cuts the last letter, T, from COMPLAINT. 'Having' and 'that's' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To complain is to grumble or express dissatisfaction.

clue.text: Feel sore in right leg joint

parts.note: the ankle joins the leg to the foot

explanation.surface: An aching pain in the right ankle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sore' looks physical, but the definition means to feel resentful; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To rankle is to cause lasting resentment, so a slight that rankles leaves one feeling sore.

clue.text: Junior officers made to climb masts

definitions.meaning: low-ranking commissioned officers, in the US Navy or formerly the British army
flags hoisted up a mast or flagpole

explanation.definitionFit: Ensigns are junior commissioned officers and also flags raised on ships' masts.
